target: audit-exp-tracker-gaps.js investigation: 68 orphan_file entries in expansion-tracker (ISS-2658)
scope_summary: Investigate the 68 orphan_file entries flagged MODERATE by audit-exp-tracker-gaps.js. Determine whether they represent genuine dropped/un-integrated work or benign legacy accumulation.
finding: BENIGN LEGACY ACCUMULATION — confirmed, no structural action needed. ISS-2658 is a re-raise of ISS-2562 (CLOSED), which analyst-baby audited on 2026-06-04 in EXP-588 and concluded "legacy accumulation, not genuine dropped work, no structural action per PROP-053-rev2." This run re-verified the conclusion against the now-68-file cohort.

evidence.prior_audit: ISS-2562 / EXP-588 (2026-06-04): concluded legacy accumulation; recommended a targeted archive sweep only if EXP-500+ orphan count exceeds 100.
evidence.sweep_threshold_check: EXP-500+ orphan count = 8, far below baby's sweep threshold of 100. No sweep warranted.
evidence.recent_orphan_issue_status: All 8 recent (EXP-560+) orphans reference issues that are now CLOSED (ISS-2476, 2512/2513/2343/2345/2515/2495, 2494, 2477, 2519, 2340/2561, 2522, 2562) — i.e. integrated/resolved work, not dropped work.
evidence.substantive_spot_check: EXP-587 (WIN-066.c7 holes) verified: its PATCH-A/PATCH-B projection-independence qualifier ("area-preserving", "~39% land vs ~19%") is present verbatim in live data/wins.json WIN-066.detail_evidence. Content demonstrably integrated, not merely issue-closed-by-other-path.

why_count_not_declining: The orphan count is monotonically non-declining BY DESIGN: integrated analyst/analyst-baby batch EXP files are never deleted (FUSE cannot unlink; no archive-sweep agent runs over monitor/analyst/expansions/), while new batch files accrue with each integration. "Count has not been declining" is expected behavior of the file-retention + tracker-pruning design, not a regression or evidence of lost work.
kernel_of_truth: The integrity agent is right that a MODERATE-severity counter that never declines is a real smell — a monitoring metric that only ratchets up is uninformative. The fix is not to chase the orphan files (they are harmless) but to recalibrate the severity heuristic.
recommendation_for_decider: Close ISS-2658 as acknowledged/no-action (duplicate resolution of ISS-2562). The 68 orphans are integrated/OBE legacy working files, verified by closed-issue cross-reference + a live-data content spot-check.
secondary_recommendation: INFRASTRUCTURE (route to tinker/integrity, do not action here): audit-exp-tracker-gaps.js currently sets severity_hint=MODERATE when total orphan_file>5. Because the cohort is monotonic-by-design, this re-raises a MODERATE issue every integrity run (ISS-2562 -> ISS-2658 -> ...). Recommend gating the MODERATE hint on the EXP-500+ orphan count (baby's 100 threshold) or on rate-of-growth, so a known-benign legacy cohort stops generating recurring MODERATE issues. A targeted archive sweep of pre-EXP-500 orphans into a JSONL would also zero the legacy bulk if FUSE-delete (allow_cowork_file_delete) is granted — operator decision.
